bet.text: Keep the turret and add storage, after a hopperless robot could not reach enough throughput to justify having none.

demand.text: The turret had to score from anywhere in the alliance zone and pass the full field, with high throughput and no dead spots.
At its provincial championship the team saw that stealing fuel pays, because whoever holds the most fuel wins; one member ranks it above the scoring period.

auto.text: A simple PID drive-to-point algorithm strings points into a path, and can move to the next point without slowing.
A match analyst points out that it shoots on the move during auto.
An observer says its auto failed against the Archimedes alliance on Einstein, and that a good one might have turned that match.

cycle.text: Fuel goes from the linear intake over the hopper's roller floor to the singulator and turret. Shots are compensated for shooting on the move. While passing, the robot keeps a minimum hopper level for the next offensive shift, and it times its shots to use that shift.

fallback.text: Buttons home the turret angle, hood and intake by hand. On low battery the robot throttles mechanisms until voltage recovers.
Holding a Purge button reverses all rollers to clear jams.

gave_up.text: Speed took priority over process, so the drawing package is messier and less complete than usual.
Testing time was reduced, every mechanism needed current limits to last a match, and dialing these in was the biggest obstacle at the first event.
In hindsight a member says dumpers such as 254's and 1678's were at least as good, and would have left more time for iteration, driver practice and programming.

changed.text: The first robot, Desperate Times, was hopperless. Its turret was reused and it carried on software development until the new robot ran three weeks later.

Desperate Times, online February 4, peaked near 14 balls per second, only in ideal conditions, against a hoped-for 20. Average throughput was substantially worse than hoppered single-stream robots'. The formal decision came February 18.
Surgical tubing was added to the intake, and the net enlarged.

outcome.text: 63-10-0 in official play; won the Hopper division; captain of the Hopper alliance on Einstein; ranked 3 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 339.00, Hopper).

solves.text: Be agile and rigid, with a low center of mass and as much volume as possible

facts.text: SDS MK5n R1 modules on Kraken motors, top speed
Chassis 25.5 in long by 29.5 in wide in 2 x 1 x 1/8 in tube, with a 1/16 in solid baseplate as shear plate
SDS spike grip wheels for traction on carpet

solves.text: Take fuel over a large area, deploy fast and withstand high energy impacts

facts.text: 2 in polycarbonate rollers in silicone tubing, X60 with a 12:30 belt
Extension: X44 through 8:40 gears and a 12 tooth pinion on a rack
Side arms are two layers of 1/4 in polycarbonate, one of them the rack, with a 2 x 1 in bash bar
A low stator current limit lets it retract like a spring in an impact
The kicker bar at the bottom is held by surgical tubing
Appropriate gearing, low fuel compression from good geometry and fairly high current limits let one motor run the rollers
A part at the intake, sprung down with surgical tubing that is not in the CAD, folds passively against the bumper as the intake retracts
The rack and its gears, made in-house, are 8 DP at a 20 degree pressure angle, for stronger teeth in the polycarbonate rack and a profile a 1/8 in end mill can cut without undercut

cost.text: Roller covers rip and are replaced as maintenance
Before the surgical tubing, balls stuck against the bumper

solves.text: Maximize fuel capacity, fill completely and feed the singulator

facts.text: Floor of 1-1/2 in polycarbonate rollers covered in silicone, one X60
The net on top is the 2025 barge net
Capacity, about
The last floor roller is bare polycarbonate, so balls slip instead of jamming

cost.text: The net had to clear the trench, and polycarbonate flex had to stay inside the frame perimeter

solves.text: Turn fuel in mass from the hopper into a single stream without jamming

facts.text: Two X44s at 12:36 drive the conveyor, with belts in a 3D printed carrier for consistent compression
The binder gives dual rubber coated timing belts; an interviewed member says a thick rubber belt below and a regular timing belt above
A vertical kicker roller on an X44 sorts fuel collisions at the quarter pipe
Dual 2 in stealth wheels feed the shooter, X60 at 16:28

functions.name: Turret

solves.text: Score from anywhere in the alliance zone and pass the full field, with no dead spots

functions.type: single-ball turret with continuously variable hood

facts.text: Plus or minus 185 degrees of rotation, with a custom printed energy chain
8 in bore X contact bearing and a 1/4 in 6061 gear; X44 through 8:40 and 10:100
4 in Fairlane shooter wheel on two X60s at 28:34
Backspin kicker of dual 2 in stealth wheels on an X44
Hood releases from 73.5 to 39.5 degrees above horizontal, X44 through 8:40 and 10:155
A magnetic proximity switch homes the turret
Passing uses the hood's lowest release angle and varies flywheel speed; shooting varies flywheel speed and hood angle

A fixed Hall effect sensor and a magnet on the turret gear seed its position while the robot is disabled, at boot or when someone moves it by hand past the sensor; until then LEDs flash purple and the turret will not auto track
The sensor triggers over a couple of degrees, so the motor's absolute rotor position sets the angle; the offset must be redone if the gearbox is taken apart
In a match the X44's internal relative encoder tracks the turret, and no camera on the turret corrects a starting error, so the first position must be close

cost.text: The backspin kicker has its own motor for spin changes in passing that were never really used, so it could have been driven from the shooter motor, although the second motor packaged quite well

functions.name: Auto Aim and Vision

solves.text: Shoot on the move, and retune quickly if fuel behaves differently at an event

functions.type: MegaTag2 pose fusion with shot compensation

facts.text: Three fixed Limelight 4s; MegaTag2 pose is fused with wheel odometry at changing confidence
Polygon zones choose pass or score and reduce hood collisions with the trench

The binder maps exit velocity to wheel speed with a hand-tuned coefficient. Interviewed members said the flywheel keeps one speed and only kicker speed and hood angle change; a later team post says flywheel speed varies too, with the kicker at a constant ratio to it
Hub shots are computed for a fixed height, so time of flight is constant and balls do not collide in the air
The pose estimator is the team's own: a squared weighted average of drivetrain odometry and the three cameras, tuned by trial and error

A camera's confidence comes from the tags in view and their average distance, and is cut in proportion to rotational velocity because MegaTag2 uses the robot's gyro; odometry confidence falls as it drives and resets on vision updates

cost.text: The PA-CF bracket of the back right Limelight was damaged three times: two partial cracks and one complete shear along the layer lines; the mounts probably should have been TPU

solves.text: Always have fuel to start the next offensive shift

facts.text: A CANrange pointed into the hopper measures the fill level
While passing, the robot fills to a minimum level first and stops passing if the level drops below it

solves.text: Use as much of the offensive shift as possible

facts.text: The robot reads game data and match time from the field system, with a manual override
When the driver asks to shoot, it decides when to shoot
The binder says red while aiming and blue when ready to shoot; an interviewed member says alliance color while shooting and otherwise red
Green lights and a rumble signal low battery; flashing yellow means passing with an empty hopper

decisions.because: throughput was not high enough to justify no storage, and other robots stored more than expected, which left fewer fuel on the floor for a hopperless robot
decisions.cost: a tighter timeline, and a drawing package messier and less complete than usual

decisions.because: its approach was the primary inspiration for nearly all aspects, and it was the most obvious change that reused as much of the first machine's development as possible
decisions.instead_of: a dumper, a dye rotor or another architecture

decisions.choice: Low current limit on the intake extension
decisions.because: the intake then retracts like a spring in an impact instead of putting a substantial load on the rack teeth
it balances speed and acceleration for short cycles
moving balls out of the opponents' zone into its hopper is more effective

decisions.choice: Fast singulation as the key to throughput
decisions.because: a member says that is the main factor for a turret

decisions.choice: Net on top of the hopper
decisions.cost: it had to clear the trench

decisions.choice: Drawings used mostly as parts lists
decisions.because: less experienced members can gather parts from them and then follow the CAD, which is far more effective than a paper drawing

decisions.choice: Choose a first architecture that can be iterated on (lesson for later seasons)
decisions.because: the team's biggest takeaway is not to roll the dice on a risky architecture based on too many assumptions

decisions.choice: Dimension drawings only for what the manufacturing process needs
decisions.because: over-dimensioning wastes time; plates cut and bent by an outside shop are made from STEP files, and CNC drawings carry overall sizes, bearing pockets and secondary operations
